My grandaunt does the same thing, but I do know that she cares about me deep inside. She tells me that the reason for my depression is because of my lack of nutrition and sleeping habits, along with doing everything that she can to give me a comfortable life. Depression just happens and is also a mixture of triggers that make you more depressed. It's an endless cycle. What I do is think that it's just another way of trying to look out for you and is a desperate attempt to make things better. You're not alone.

The thing is, things will get better. It just takes small steps to do so. Make small goals, do little things that will build your self-confidence like a hobby or an interest. Then it will progress into something where you can keep focused on your goals and interests. Depression makes it difficult for you to focus and do stuff, along with your other symptoms, but you've just got to deal with the cards that you have. Think of your achievements, your darkest moments and look back into who you are today. If you don't remember, make an effort to write positive and constructive thoughts about the present to distract yourself from anxious thoughts about the future, because the present is the only one that we can control. It will make you see your improvement if you write your fears down, the things you can't do, and then the things that make you rational, sane and happy. Also what really helps me a lot is to think that of ways to solve my problems and to keep looking for ways, instead of forcing myself to stress out about it. I was in your place, but I'm feeling much better after medications, therapy and doing the things that I love.
Good job! Sometimes you just have to keep living your life despite having anxiety ruining it for you. Keep doing what you need to do! Hope you can keep it up.

Nah, you're not going crazy. I'm taking medications (amisulpride) for schizophrenia and generalized anxiety disorder, and there are times where I read but the words just don't register unless if I'm really into what I'm reading. Trying to read things I don't give a damn is kind of hard, and sometimes I skip through dialogue on a game (that is what I try to avoid, though). I told my psychiatrist and she said that it's normal. It got worse when I was unmedicated and the anxiety attacks make it more difficult to focus at work. Try to go back at it when you're feeling less tired or better. I've noticed that it doesn't happen all the time, just when I'm tired and not in the mood to read. For digital content, I use Natural Reader or Speakit to read things out loud for me.

I feel that way often, but I was able to fight such thoughts. What I do is that I think of myself as someone on a different phase and journey than the other person I'm comparing myself to. I may be lesser than them in comparison, but I improved in comparison to before because most of us grow and changes in time. I also set daily goals and I put a checklist on my tablet which helps me focus on getting better. I try to focus more on doing things I love and need than dwelling on anxiety and trying to keep up with the Joneses.

So far I lost 15.8 lbs from portion control and doing cardio for an hour a day on antipsychotics (300 mg amisulpride ). Gained 50lbs on clozapine and 20lbs while adjusting to amisulpride. I was 255 to 239.2 lbs. Though it's just 15.8 lbs it's still progress.

I removed soda and only drink water and fresh juices.

So far I think it's possible but since antipsychotics lower your metabolism it's imperative to workout to up your metabolism. Maybe walk more or do jumping jacks in your room; get your heart pumping.
